To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have calculated the J/ψ dissociation cross section by pions using QCD sum rule methods.
the dissociation of J/ψ by pions is important for the suppression of J/ψ in the quark–glue plasma.

the J/ψ dissociation cross section by thermal pions at temperatures of relevance in heavy-ion collisions is of the order of 0.2–4 mb, and that the dissociation cross sections of J/ψ by pions and by quark–glus plasma are similar.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the J/ψ suppression in heavy-ion collisions.
the study of charmonium production in the hot and dense medium produced in relativistic heavy ion collisions.
the study of J/ψ dissociation in QCD by means of QCD sum rules and the thermal average of this cross section at finite temperature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the framework of QCD sum rules, we find that the dissociation of the J/ψ by pions is not a negligible process, and it is not negligible compared to the dissociation by quark–glon plasma.
the dissociation of J/ψ by pions is not the dominant source of the suppression in J/ψ production at SPS energies, but it could become important at higher energies.
the J/ψ dissociation cross section through pion interactions is of the order of 0.3 mb at T≈150 MeV and that this cross section does not depend significantly on the temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the J/ψ suppression by pion dissociation is not large enough to account for the observed J/ψ suppression in the heavy ion collisions at RHIC and at LHC.
the dissociation of J/ψ by comoving pion gas is not negligible.
the J/ψ dissociation cross section is not large enough to explain all the J/ψ suppression observed in heavy ion collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cross section for the dissociation of a J/ψ by a thermal pion is much smaller than what has been previously assumed.
the dissociation cross section by comoving pion is much larger than that by quark–glubon plasma, which is a factor 10 smaller.
the cross section for the J/ ψ dissociation by pion is small, and therefore, it can be neglected in the analysis of the J/ ψ suppression in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
